executive_summary: S&P 500 closed at a record 7,365 yesterday (+1.46%) and futures point to an additional firm open as a US-Iran ceasefire memorandum, routed via Islamabad, triggers a peace-trade unwind across oil, defense, and tankers. WTI crashed 13% to test $89 before stabilizing above $95; Brent followed to $96 then bounced to $101. The rally beneficiaries are duration, growth, and oil-consumers — Nasdaq futures lead +0.94% with semis (AMD +16% yesterday on results) extending. Fed remains on hold at 3.50-3.75% with four dissents in April (first time since 1992), and Kevin Warsh is set for confirmation May 15. McDonald's reports pre-market (consensus $2.75 EPS, +3.7% comps) into a 52-week-low chart.

macro_events.title: US-Iran ceasefire memorandum routed through Pakistan triggers oil collapse
macro_events.causal_chain: US transmits 1-page MOU to Tehran via Islamabad → markets price 70%+ probability of Strait of Hormuz reopening → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs collapse from $4M+/voyage → Asian refiners cancel Cape of Good Hope rerouting (saves +12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → spot crude floods back into Asia-Pacific basin → Brent/WTI structure flips from backwardation toward contango → Brent -12% intraday to $96.73, WTI -13.3% to $88.66 → US gasoline futures -9% → 5Y breakeven inflation drops 12bps → 10Y nominal yield eases 6bps to 4.37% → growth/duration outperform value/cyclicals
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Persian Gulf shipping lanes; Asia-Pacific oil importers (China, India, Japan, Korea); European LNG (Qatar exposure); Russia (oil revenue collapse pressures Kremlin budget built on $60 Brent — now potentially below $90 sustainably)
macro_events.historical_analog: 2003 Iraq invasion: oil spiked then collapsed 25% within 6 weeks of major combat ending; tanker rates -40% in one quarter. 2019 Abqaiq attack saw +15% Brent in 24h fully reversed within 10 days.
macro_events.counterargument: Trump cautioned the deal is 'a big assumption' Iran will accept; UAE attacks reportedly continued during the announcement. Historical base rate for Middle East ceasefires breaking within 90 days is ~40%. A failed deal triggers immediate +$15 Brent reflex move.

macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — Bunds, Gilts, JGBs all participate; EM local-currency debt (INR, IDR, TRY) rallies as oil-import burden eases
macro_events.historical_analog: Jan 2019 oil collapse: 10Y fell from 2.78% to 2.55% in 3 weeks, S&P +12% same window. Aug 2015 commodity rout produced similar duration rally.
macro_events.counterargument: April 29 FOMC saw four dissents (first since Oct 1992) — three members opposing dovish language plus Miran wanting cuts. The committee is internally fragile; a hawkish Warsh testimony May 15 could spike yields back through 4.50% on policy-uncertainty premium.
